cards.explanation: The answer is that they ask where He wants them to prepare it. On the first day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the disciples ask, "Where do You want us to prepare for You to eat the Passover?" (Matthew 26:17). They don't just show up hungry and hope for the best. A crew that asks the question before the feast starts is a crew I'd hire.

The answer is house, friends. Jesus tells them to say, "I will keep the Passover with My disciples at your house." (Matthew 26:18). The meal happens under a roof, at a certain man's place in the city. Whoever that man is, he's about to get some very special company.

The answer is False, friends. Calm is the opposite of what happens. The text says, "They were deeply grieved…" (Matthew 26:22). Then they begin to ask Him one after another, "Surely not I, Lord?" I think the whole room went quiet before the questions started.

The answer is bowl. Jesus says, "The one who has dipped his hand into the bowl with Me will betray Me." (Matthew 26:23). He's talking about someone sitting right there at the meal. That's what makes it so heavy.

The answer is that what happens to Him was already in Scripture, friends. Jesus says the Son of Man will go "…just as it is written about Him…" (Matthew 26:24). It means what's coming was already written. He says it right in the middle of the meal.

The answer is True, and it's a heavy line. Jesus says, "…woe to that man by whom He is betrayed. It would be better for him if he had not been born." (Matthew 26:24). I think this one hurts to hear. There's no joke to make here, so I'll just let it sit.

The answer is "You have said it yourself." Judas asks, "Surely not I, Rabbi?" and Jesus answers, "You have said it yourself." (Matthew 26:25). Judas, one of the Twelve, asks a question like the ones the others asked. The answer he gets is short and plain.

The answer is His body, friends. Jesus gives the bread to the disciples and says, "Take and eat; this is My body." (Matthew 26:26). He takes it, blesses it, breaks it and hands it over. It's one of the most important moments at this table.

The two answers are blood and forgiveness, friends. Jesus says, "This is My blood of the covenant…" (Matthew 26:28). He's giving them the cup and telling them what it means. Then He says His blood "…is poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins." (Matthew 26:28). That's the heart of what He's handing them: forgiveness for many, and the cup goes to all of them.

The answer is until He drinks it anew in His Father's kingdom. Jesus says He won't drink of the fruit of the vine "…until that day when I drink it anew with you in My Father’s kingdom." (Matthew 26:29). He doesn't leave it at goodbye. He points to a day He'll drink it again with them.

The answer is True, friends. The text says that when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives (Matthew 26:30). After a night with that much weight in it, they still sing together. I think that's worth noticing.

The answer is scattered, friends. Jesus quotes, "I will strike the Shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered." (Matthew 26:31). He says it's written, and He's telling them ahead of time. The sheep part is about all of them.

The answer is that He'll go ahead of them into Galilee. Jesus says, "But after I have risen, I will go ahead of you into Galilee." (Matthew 26:32). Right after the hard news, He talks about what comes after He has risen. He keeps going.

The answer is deny, friends. Jesus tells Peter, "this very night, before the rooster crows, you will deny Me three times." (Matthew 26:34). Peter is one of the Twelve, and he had just said he'd never fall away. I think that stings.

The answer is False, friends. Peter says, "Even if I have to die with You, I will never deny You." and then the text says, "…all the other disciples said the same thing." (Matthew 26:35). Peter is just the one the text quotes. All of them are making big promises.
